[NOREF] Attemping to Speed up Cypress (#2569)

* skip compression and only upload fialed tests

* splitting teh cypress tests to shards to parallelize the tests

* wip

* [NOREF] Fix cy.localLogin detached-element race

The login form can re-render between a mid-chain `.should()` and the
following action, which left the action holding a detached element and
failed specs in the beforeEach session setup.

Use one cy.get() per action so each re-queries the DOM, assert the typed
value, and drop the blind cy.wait(500). Verified stable over 18 login-heavy
runs under heavy machine load, including the assessment-role path.

* [NOREF] Create notification triggers via API in notification spec

Add createDiscussion and addCollaborator cy.tasks that call the same
GraphQL mutations as the UI forms (plan IDs are looked up by name), and use
them to set up the events in three notification tests instead of clicking
through the forms. Those forms are covered by discussions.spec.js and
collaborator.spec.js.

- Reload with cy.visit('/notifications') after an API-created event: the nav
  bar polls every 5s and shares a cache with the page, so a client-side
  navigation shows a stale list until the next poll.
- Wait for the settings-saved toast before triggering the event so the call
  can't race the preference save.

notification.spec.js: ~94s -> ~70s (3 interleaved runs each).

* [NOREF] Balance Cypress shards by measured spec durations

Weight the shard split by per-spec durations from cypress/spec-timings.json
instead of line count. Specs missing from the file get the average, and the
script falls back to line counts if the file is absent.

Projected 4-shard loads go from 114-179s (65s spread) to 153-160s (7s spread).
Timings come from a local run and should be refreshed from CI.

* Revert "[NOREF] Fix cy.localLogin detached-element race"

This reverts commit 9f65be38a.

The detached-element failures it targeted only appeared in a run where two
full suites overlapped on the same database, and the previous login code
passed a clean full run with no login failures. The change saved ~0.5s per
spec, and removing the cy.wait(500) may expose a late re-render of the login
form (typed values lost before submit). An interleaved comparison showed no
difference between the two versions (10/10 each), but one earlier batch with
the new code failed 4/12 at login, so restore the known-good behavior.

* [NOREF] Document Okta login test requirements

Explain what the "logs in with okta" test needs, locally and in CI: the
build-time VITE_OKTA_REDIRECT_LOGIN_ENABLED=true flag, the OKTA_TEST_*
credentials, and network access to the Okta test IdP. Locally the flag
defaults to false in .envrc, which makes cy.login() fail after retrying.

* [NOREF] Fix stale MTO status after marking ready for review

The mutation's refetchQueries refetches GetModelToOperationsMatrix, but
Apollo deduplicates identical in-flight queries. If the page's own matrix
query was still in flight when the mutation finished, the refetch attached to
that request, which pre-dates the mutation, so the status tag stayed "In
progress" until a reload.

Disable query deduplication for this refetch via context. This was the cause
of the flaky "MTO is marked Ready for Review" test in notification.spec.js:
it failed ~4 in 12 isolated runs before, and 0 in 40 runs after.

* Stop notification settings and Cypress from racing the save

* random commit

* Revert "random commit"

This reverts commit 38541e4b1813ffa428184893829949a883330d13.

* Report the e2e_tests status after all Cypress shards finish

Branch protection waits on run_tests / e2e_tests, but the matrix jobs only report shard names, so that required check never arrives.

* Judge the e2e rollup from the shard result, not outcome

A matrix job leaves needs.*.outcome empty, so the rollup failed after every shard passed. Read result instead, and do not ignore shard failures.

* Stop the Okta login test from submitting an expired OTP.

Wait for the authenticator field and a fresh TOTP window before typing the code, so a retry is not required when the 30s window is about to roll.

* Record per-spec Cypress durations so CI shards stay balanced.

commits.message:
feat(misc#378): log the TLS key exchange group on the SMTP and Kion hops (#614)

Part of
[ztmf-misc#378](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc/issues/378)
· Epic [ztmf#572](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/issues/572) ·
Stacked on [ztmf!613](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/pull/613)

### Summary

pqc 4 measures each hop behind the ALB. Most far ends were probed
directly on 2026-10-13, but two can't be reached from the ops task: the
CMS SMTP relay (587, STARTTLS) and Kion. Instead of widening the ops
task's security group, this PR logs the negotiated group from the
clients that use those hops, with the `tlslog.Verifier` hook from
ztmf!613: `tls handshake: hop=smtp ...` after STARTTLS in `mail.Send`,
and `tls handshake: hop=kion ...` on the Kion key rotation call. Both
clients already offer `X25519MLKEM768` through Go's defaults, so the
logged group is what the far end accepted.

### Changes

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `backend/cmd/api/internal/mail/mail.go` | Always passes a `tls.Config`
to `smtp.DialStartTLS`, with `RootCAs` from the SMTP config and
`VerifyConnection: tlslog.Verifier("smtp")`. A nil `RootCAs` still means
the system roots, and go-smtp fills in `ServerName` from the host, so
the connection behaves as before. |
| `backend/cmd/lambda-kion-key-rotate/internal/kion/client.go` | The
HTTP client uses a clone of `http.DefaultTransport` with
`VerifyConnection: tlslog.Verifier("kion")`. The 30 second timeout and
the no-redirect rule are unchanged. |
| `backend/cmd/lambda-kion-key-rotate/internal/kion/client_test.go` |
New test: a rotate call against a TLS test server logs the `hop=kion`
line. |

### Verified

- `make test-unit`, `make test-integration`, and `make test-e2e` pass.
- The SMTP path has no test harness; the client-side hook itself is
covered by `TestVerifierOnClient` in ztmf!613.

### After merge

- Kion: the rotation Lambda runs daily at 06:00 UTC in dev and prod, so
the `hop=kion` line shows up the next morning in its log group.
- SMTP: the `hop=smtp` line appears on the next email send; one mass
email in dev produces it.
- Probe results so far: AWS endpoints accept `X25519MLKEM768`; Aurora PG
16, Okta, Entra and Kion (from outside the VPC) do not. The full table
goes into `docs/pqc-readiness.md` in a follow-up.

chore(misc#430): move the root Terraform module to AWS provider v6 (#618)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#430

### What and why

[ztmf!617](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/pull/617) sets
CloudFront's `minimum_protocol_version` to `TLSv1.3_2025`. Danny found
in review that provider 5.89 validates that field against an SDK enum
ending at `TLSv1.2_2021`, so the dev apply would reject it. The value
first ships in provider v6.9.0 (CloudFront SDK v1.52.0), and no 5.x
release has it. This moves the root module to `~> 6.68.0`, the current
release, so ztmf!617 can land after it.

commits.message:
feat(misc#391): add score_revisions with answer history and undo (#596)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#391 (epic ztmf-misc#307).

> [!NOTE]
> **Stacked on #595.** The base is #595's branch, not `main`, so the
diff excludes that PR's transaction rework. Retarget to `main` once #595
merges. CI first runs then, because it only triggers on PRs to `main`.

## Summary

`scores` is updated in place, so an overwritten answer cannot be
recovered, and `events` cannot help:
- its payload is the row *after* the write;
- the rollover records nothing;
- `GET /events` is closed to ISSOs.

This PR:
- adds `score_revisions`, append-only and written in the same
transaction as the answer (#595's transaction);
- adds `GET /scores/{scoreid}/revisions` and `POST
/scores/{scoreid}/revisions/undo`;
- adds the API's first 409, carrying `code: "REVISION_CONFLICT"`,
documented through a doc-only `apiError { error, code }`. That keeps
`code` out of every success schema.

It has no backfill and leaves `events` unchanged. ztmf-ui#740 is the UI.

## Undo rules

| Decision | Why |
|---|---|
| Undo **appends** a `kind='undo'` revision | Who undid what stays
auditable. An undo is terminal: one step, no redo, so repeated clicks
cannot fill the trail with repeats |
| Only the **head** is undoable | It keeps `expected_head_revisionid`
unambiguous |
| `expected_head_revisionid` is **required** | Without a token, a
destructive action is last-write-wins. A stale token gets a 409 |
| Undoing a `confirm` **un-confirms** | The answer is untouched and the
status returns to `not_started`, which re-enables Confirm |

These heads are refused with a field-level 400 carrying a server-owned
reason. They are not 409s, because refreshing returns the same head and
a retry can never succeed:
- `create`: there is no earlier value.
- `undo`: undo is terminal.
- `translate`: reserved for ztmf-misc#397, so a re-pin cannot be
reverted across versions.
- **Drift:** the row no longer matches the head's `new` side, meaning
something wrote it without recording a revision.
- No history at all.

`undoable` and its `reason` depend on the reader: read-only roles and
closed calls see every row as not undoable. That lets the UI show
history read-only without knowing the role matrix.

## Schema

- **Denormalised `fismasystemid` and `datacallid`**, so reads can be
scoped to an OpDiv without a join. That scoping is what `events` lacks.
- **Denormalised `functionid`**, copied from `scores.functionid`. It
keeps history readable once #397 re-points a cycle at another catalog
version.
- **No `versionid` yet.** It cannot be derived later once #397 re-pins
open cycles. **#394 should add `versionid` and `root_functionid` here**
in its migration.
- **No FK on `prev_/new_functionoptionid`.** History must survive a
catalog delete, so reads `LEFT JOIN` for labels.
- **`revision_no` is allocated as `MAX+1`** under the score row's `FOR
UPDATE` lock. `UNIQUE (scoreid, revision_no)` is only a backstop.
- **Recorded in the Go write path, not a trigger.** A trigger cannot see
the acting user, and seed inserts carry none. Because writes go through
the Go path, the rollover and read-through PUTs record nothing, and both
are asserted.

## Consequences to call out

- **Progress can go down.** Undoing the first edit of a carried-forward
answer returns it to `not_started`, so the updated count drops by one.
This is correct, but it has never happened before.
- **Undo stamps `scores.last_updated_at`** (`clock_timestamp()`, like
Save and Confirm). So an answer can show a recent "last updated" next to
an unconfirmed chip. Migration 0066 updates the column comment to name
undo as a writer.

## Verification

- `make test-integration` passes on a fresh DB. `make test-e2e` runs 280
Emberfall cases with 0 failures. Unit tests, `go build` and `go vet` are
clean.
- `make generate-openapi` is idempotent. Redocly reports the same 10
warnings as `main`.
- Integration tests cover:
  - what records and what does not;
  - restore, un-confirm and the progress decrement;
  - conflict and guard refusals, including drift and `translate`;
  - read-only readers;
  - 8 concurrent Saves numbered 1..9;
- concurrent history reads, bounded so the connection pool cannot
deadlock.
- #595's race-loser test now also asserts one `update` revision and no
`create`.
- **Emberfall does not cover the successful undo.** The request body
needs the live head id, and Emberfall templates URLs only. Emberfall
pins the history shape and every refusal. Go covers the happy path end
to end.
- `TestFindUsersLastSeenIntegration` is hardened. It picked the busiest
user, which this PR's fixtures made the seed OWNER, whose id fails
`isValidUUID`. It now picks the busiest user with a valid id.

## Merge, deploy, release

- **Migration `0066`.** If ztmf-misc#394 merges first, whichever lands
second renumbers.
- **Deploy:** `ztmf` first, before any undo UI.
- **Release gates (not merge gates):**
  - Records and privacy sign-off on retaining attributed answer history.
- @danielbowne's acknowledgement that `score_revisions` stays out of the
Snowflake `data-sync` allowlist. It holds a second attributed copy of
every justification.

## Deliberately not changed

- **History returns 403 rather than 404** for a row the caller cannot
see. That matches `/confirm`. Hiding existence belongs in a sweep across
all score endpoints.
- **Undo is still offered for an option deleted since.** The undo then
fails as a generic 400. Fixing it belongs with ztmf-misc#396, which
makes option deletes routine.
- **History is capped at the 200 newest revisions.** The cap is
unreachable in practice, and the response is an object, so a `total` can
be added later.

feat(misc#377): log the TLS key exchange group of each API handshake (#613)

Part of CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#377 · Epic
[ztmf#572](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/issues/572)

### Summary

The API now logs one line per TLS handshake it accepts, naming the hop,
the protocol version and the key exchange group, for example `tls
handshake: hop=alb version=TLS 1.3 group=X25519MLKEM768`. This is the
evidence for pqc 3: the load balancer to API hop is expected to switch
from classical `X25519` to hybrid `X25519MLKEM768` when the internal ALB
listener moves to the post-quantum policy in a follow-up PR. Landing the
logging first records the "before" in dev and prod, so the policy change
shows up as a flip in the logs rather than an inference.

### Changes

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `backend/internal/tlslog/tlslog.go` | New `Verifier(hop)`, which
returns a `VerifyConnection` hook that logs the hop, negotiated version
and group and never rejects a connection. It sits in `backend/internal`
so the Lambdas can use it too, and works on server and client configs. |
| `backend/cmd/api/main.go` | Sets `VerifyConnection:
tlslog.Verifier("alb")` on the existing server `tls.Config`. The plain
HTTP path (local dev, PR environments) is unchanged. |
| `backend/internal/tlslog/tlslog_test.go` | Server side: a TLS server
with the hook, connected once forcing `X25519MLKEM768` and once forcing
`X25519`. Client side: the hook on a client config against servers
limited to each group. Checks the logged line in every case. |

### Decisions

- **Labeled by hop.** The same hook covers the outbound hops in the pqc
4 PR stacked on this one (`hop=smtp`, `hop=kion`), so one CloudWatch
filter on `tls handshake:` finds all of them.
- **Per handshake, not per request.** The ALB reuses backend
connections, so a per-request line would repeat the same value on every
call. The hook runs once per new connection.
- **Volume.** ALB health checks open a new connection every 30 seconds
per ALB node, so expect a few thousand short lines a day in each
environment's API log group.
- **No PR environment evidence.** PR environment tasks serve plain HTTP
behind nginx, so the hook does not run there. It runs in dev, impl, and
prod, where the API terminates TLS from the ALB.

### Verified

- Tests pass on the host with `-race`. They also confirm the group is
populated by the time the hook runs, on both the server and client side.
- `make test-unit`, `make test-integration`, and `make test-e2e` pass.

### After merge

Dev and prod API logs should show `hop=alb ... group=X25519` for
connections from the ALB, which is the pre-change baseline for the
listener policy PR.

commits.message:
refactor(scores): write answers and their audit events in one transaction (#595)

Prerequisite for CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#391 (epic ztmf-misc#307).
**Draft** — no rush to merge. Carries no migration. Now synced with
`main` through #609, so it also carries #594's natural-key resolution
and #609's `last_updated_at` into the transaction (see below).

## Summary

`score_revisions` has to be written in the same transaction as the
answer it describes, or it inherits the exact unreliability that makes
`events` unusable as history. Nothing in the score write path is
transactional today, so that transaction has to exist first. This is
that change and nothing else — no new table, no new endpoint, no API
change.

- **Moves** `Score.Save` and `Score.Confirm` into one transaction each,
following the `RestoreUser` idiom, with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the
score row
- **Hand-writes** the `events` row inside that transaction, because
`queryRow`'s automatic `recordEvent` hook no longer fires for this path
- **Closes** the no-op race that `scoreUpdateIsNoOp`'s own doc comment
documented and tolerated
- **Fixes** an event-ordering inversion the move introduced, caught by a
new test rather than by review
- **Carries** #594's natural-key resolve and same-question check, and
#609's `last_updated_at`, into that transaction, replacing #594's 23505
retry with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`

## Why the event has to move too

`recordEvent` fires from `queryRow` *after* the write, on a second
pooled connection, fire-and-forget with its error discarded. Four
readers depend on the row it writes:

| Reader | Matches on |
|---|---|
| `lookupScoreAudit` | `resource = 'public.scores'`, newest by
`createdat` |
| `FindScores` lateral | same |
| `scorediff.go` | same |
| `scoreprogress.go` | same **plus** `action IN ('created','updated')` |

Every one of them `LEFT JOIN`s, so a missing or mislabelled event yields
NULL rather than an error — attribution goes dark estate-wide with
nothing failing. `insertScoreEvent` therefore reproduces `recordEvent`
exactly: the `public.scores` literal is hoisted to a constant, actions
come from `eventActionCreated`/`eventActionUpdated`, the payload is the
same `*Score` off the same `RETURNING` list through the same
`RowToStructByNameLax`, and it stays actor-gated so a context with no
user still records nothing.

`Save` reads that event straight back through `lookupScoreAudit` to
stamp `last_edited_*`. Out of transaction, that read races its own
write.

## The ordering inversion

Worth reading even if you skim the rest — this was a real defect in the
first version of this branch, not a hypothetical.

`events.createdat` defaults to `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, which in Postgres is
**transaction start** time. Once the event moved inside a transaction
that may sit waiting on `FOR UPDATE`:

```
writer 0: BEGIN (t=1) ──── blocked on lock ──────── writes, COMMIT (t=9)  ← wins in scores
writer 3:      BEGIN (t=2) ─ lock ─ writes, COMMIT (t=3)                  ← event looks newest
```

The row holds writer 0's answer; the newest event by `createdat` is
writer 3's. All four readers order by `createdat DESC`, so
`last_edited_by` would name the editor whose answer had just been
overwritten.

This ordering used to be *incidentally* correct — `recordEvent` ran
after the score had committed, in its own short transaction, so start
time was effectively insert time. The fix is to write `createdat`
explicitly as `clock_timestamp()`; because the insert happens while the
row lock is still held, event order now matches commit order by
construction. Pinned by
`TestScoreConcurrentSavesAgreeWithEventLogIntegration`, which is what
caught it.

## What the lock buys, and what it costs

`Save`'s no-op guard now compares against the `FOR UPDATE` row instead
of one the controller preloaded, so "unchanged" is decided against the
values the `UPDATE` would overwrite and holds until commit.

`scoreUpdateIsNoOp`'s doc conceded the old comparison could not promise
that: *"a concurrent writer could land a real change in the gap."* Its
consequence was understated, though — a read-through PUT comparing
against a stale snapshot skips a write it should have performed, which
drops the submitted answer rather than merely lagging the response.

The cost is real and stated in the commit: a read-through PUT — the
questionnaire's hottest path, issued on every Next click — goes from one
round trip to `BEGIN` + `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` + `COMMIT`, holding a
row lock throughout. **Do not reclaim it by comparing against a
preloaded row before opening the transaction**; that is precisely the
race being closed, and it reads as a harmless optimization. There is a
comment on `lockScore` saying so.

`WithCurrentScore` and `scoreUpdateIsNoOp` are removed as a consequence.
#594 re-added both on `main` to spare the hot-path PUT a second read, so
this PR removes them a second time. With the locked read in place the
preloaded row has no remaining use: the same-question check now compares
against the `FOR UPDATE` row too, and an option that looks load-bearing
but is not would be worse than the extra read.

## Carrying #594 and #609 into the transaction

Merging `main` conflicted in `scores.go` only, and neither side was
correct: this branch had the transaction but none of #594's logic, and
`main` had #594 and #609 but no transaction. The resolution keeps this
PR's structure and ports the three behaviours into it.

- **A create locks by natural key.** With `scoreid == 0`, `Save` takes
`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on `(fismasystemid, datacallid, functionid)`. If a
row exists, the create carries on as an update of it and records
`updated`, as on `main`. One round trip resolves and locks
- **No row: `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (fismasystemid, datacallid,
functionid) DO NOTHING`.** #594 retried a 23505 by re-entering `save`.
Inside a transaction that can't work, because the failed `INSERT` aborts
the tx and anything after it fails `25P02`. `DO NOTHING` waits for a
concurrent insert of the same answer to commit instead of failing, so
the transaction stays usable: the loser locks the winner's row and lands
as an update, in the same transaction. #594's tests argued against `ON
CONFLICT DO UPDATE` because `recordEvent` derived the action from the
statement type, so an update would have logged `created`. This PR
records the action explicitly, so that no longer applies. The conflict
target names 0061's index only, so any other unique violation still
errors. This does make `Save` depend on that index existing: 0061
re-runs `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` on every boot, and the tests
that drop it never call `Save` while it is gone
- **The same-question check uses the locked row.** `lockScore` now also
returns the row's `functionid`, beside the `Score` rather than as a new
field, because `Score` is both the API response and the event payload.
The check then needs only the option's `functionid`, and runs only when
a caller-named row's option changed. A create that resolved by natural
key is the same question by construction
- **Every lookup runs on the transaction.** No helper takes a second
pooled connection while the tx holds one, which is the pool-exhaustion
shape #596 already had to fix once. #594's `findScoreIDByNaturalKey` and
`scoreAnswersSameQuestion` are gone, replaced by `lockScoreByNaturalKey`
and `functionIDOfOption`
- **`last_updated_at` rides all three write statements**: the `INSERT`,
the `UPDATE` and `Confirm`'s `UPDATE`, in the same statement as `status
= 'done'`, per #609. Written as `clock_timestamp()` rather than #609's
`now()`: inside a transaction `now()` is the start time, so a writer
that waited on the lock would stamp an earlier time than the writer it
overwrote. Same fix as `events.createdat` above

## Behaviour changes

Two, both deliberate, both worth a reviewer's attention:

1. **An `events` insert failure now fails the whole write.** It used to
be logged and swallowed. A committed answer with no trace of who changed
it is the state score history exists to eliminate — but this does mean a
broken `events` table takes the questionnaire down rather than degrading
quietly. Pinned by `TestScoreWriteRollsBackWhenEventFailsIntegration`.
2. **`Confirm` takes no `FOR UPDATE`.** Its `WHERE status <> 'done'` is
atomic and takes its own row lock, so a separate lock would add a round
trip and guard nothing. Noted in a comment because #391 changes it —
allocating `revision_no` as `MAX+1` needs the lock held across the read.

No API change. `emberfall_tests.yml` is **unmodified**, which is the
actual proof the contract did not move.

## Verification

- [x] `make test-integration` green against an unmodified
`_test_data_empire.sql`
- [x] `make test-e2e` — 265 Emberfall cases, 0 failed,
`emberfall_tests.yml` untouched
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean; no new `gofmt` deviations
(`controller/scores.go` was already listed on `main`)
- [x] `make test-unit` green
- [x] `openapi.yaml` is byte-identical to `main`, and `make
generate-openapi` produces no diff
- [x] Mutation-checked rather than trusted green: changing
`scoresEventResource` to `"scores"` fails both new event tests
- [x] Race test run 12× consecutively after the `clock_timestamp()` fix
- [x] After the `main` merge: the concurrency tests, the new race test
and #594's natural-key and same-question tests each run 10×, all green
- [x] The new race test, mutation-checked: removing the `ON CONFLICT`
clause fails it on every run

New coverage in
`backend/internal/model/scores_txwrite_integration_test.go`:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `TestScoreWriteRecordsEventInSameTransactionIntegration` | create →
`created`, update → `updated`, no-op → no event; audit stamp resolves |
| `TestScoreConcurrentSavesAgreeWithEventLogIntegration` | the surviving
row equals the newest event; no write loses its event |
| `TestScoreWriteRollsBackWhenEventFailsIntegration` | a failed event
rolls back the answer, on both insert and update paths |

And in `scores_uniqueanswer_integration_test.go`:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `TestSaveCreateLosingToInFlightInsertIntegration` | deterministic: a
rival transaction holds an uncommitted insert of the same answer; `Save`
blocks on it, then updates the rival's row with one `updated` event and
no `created` |

`TestScoreWriteRollsBackWhenEventFailsIntegration` needs no fault
injection: `events.userid` is a real FK, so a well-formed but
non-existent user id makes the event insert raise 23503 while the score
statement stays valid — the exact shape of the failure being guarded
against.

## Relationship to ztmf-misc#391 and #594

- **Does not deliver CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#391.** No
`score_revisions`, no history endpoint, no undo. This is the transaction
those land in
- **Builds on #594 / ztmf#491, which has merged.** Its natural-key
resolution now runs inside this transaction, and its 23505 retry is
replaced by `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (above). No migration here, so no
numbering interaction
- **Preserves #609 / ztmf-misc#426.** `last_updated_at` is written by
the same statements as `status`
- `scoreTx` / `lockScore` / `writeScore` / `insertScoreEvent` are the
single hook #391 and ztmf-misc#397 both write through, rather than each
rediscovering the transaction and event discipline

commits.message:
feat(dashboard): replace the dashboard stat tiles with an action-led summary (#749)

* feat(dashboard): system-scoped summary band for ISSOs and ISSMs

Home's stat tiles describe an estate - highest score, lowest score, how many
sit at Optimal. Across three systems those name two of the three and answer
nothing, and nothing on the page says what needs doing before the deadline.

Home now picks its summary by tier. Admin tiers keep StatisticsBlocks
unchanged; ISSO, ISSM and System Delegate get a band built around what needs
their action. Delegates are answers-only, so the target-maturity worklist is
withheld from them rather than offering a backlog they would 403 on.

The headline row - overall score and the KPI tiles - is always visible. The
detail sits behind one toggle, collapsed by default so the systems table stays
within reach, and the choice is remembered. Panels with no underlying data are
dropped; panels holding an all-clear are kept, since "every system has
progress" is an answer rather than an absence.

Four per-system derivations no page carried before: questionnaire progress with
the unconfirmed carry-forward count called out (ztmf#659 - a cycle is seeded
with last cycle's answers, so a system can read as finished and register
nothing), systems with no target maturity asserted, per-system movement against
the prior call, and each system's weakest pillar.

Scoping needs no new endpoints: the backend already narrows /scores/aggregate
and /scores/progress to AssignedFismaSystems, so useOpDivDashboardData with no
OpDiv filter is exactly this caller's scope. /users is 403 for these tiers, so
nothing roster-shaped is requested.

Supporting changes:

- Home reads scores and progress through the query layer instead of axios +
  useEffect, so it shares cache entries with the band rather than fetching
  every call twice.
- useOpDivDashboardData takes an options object: a cadence override, since an
  ISSO whose systems are all CMS follows the quarterly calls rather than the
  annual ones, and a detail gate so the collapsed band does not pay for the
  score history it will not draw.
- The reused cards take a scopeNoun. They said "this OpDiv", which misdescribes
  a caller whose scope is their assignments.

Refs #747

* feat(dashboard): give every tier the summary band, and bound its lists

The band replaces the estate-wide stat tiles for everyone rather than only for
system-scoped tiers. Those tiles described a population - highest, lowest, how
many at Optimal - which answered nothing for a reader holding three systems
and little more for one holding a thousand. The band describes whatever
/fismasystems returned for the caller, which the backend has already narrowed,
so one page reads the same whoever opens it. Admins who want per-OpDiv depth
go to the OpDiv dashboard, which is built for it.

That makes the per-system panels reachable at OpDiv scale, so completion,
movement, weakest pillar and targets now cap through the same
useExpandableRows the OpDiv panels use rather than rendering every row.

Movement is withheld unless a system is actually scored in both calls. With a
prior call but nothing paired, every row read "not scored" - a card saying
nothing the hero's "no prior call to compare" does not already say.

StatisticsBlocks goes with its last consumer.

Refs #747

* fix(dashboard): trim the summary band and point its tiles at the table

The expanded detail keeps only the score trend; the per-system panels
repeated what the systems table already shows.

- Not started and Answers to confirm turn on the table's "Not updated
  only" filter and jump to it, when the open call is in view.
  FismaTable's notUpdatedOnly is optionally controlled for this.
- The band never fetches pillar aggregates, and fetches history only
  when expanded.
- Shared headline pieces move to components/ScoreSummary (OpDivHero ->
  ScoreHero, OpDivKpiRow -> SummaryKpiRow); OpDiv-only ones stay put.
- Weakest-pillar, movement, completion and target panels and their
  derivations are removed.

* fix(dashboard): address review feedback on the summary band

- Not started and Answers to confirm count only open-call rows while the
  open call is in view, so the tiles match the table filter they turn on.
- A failed score or progress read hides the band's figures behind a
  notice instead of reading as an all-clear.
- Tile copy reads for any scope, the band heading is scope-neutral, and
  the score and trend headings nest under it as h3.
- Drop issue numbers from new comments; point the stale stat-tile
  comment at the summary band; correct the describeChild comment.

* fix(dashboard): scope the band's completion figures to the open call

- While the open call is in view, the completion summary skips closed-call
  rows entirely, so the Not started denominator, the "underway" hint and
  the progress figure describe the same systems the table filter shows.
- Give the systems table a visually hidden h2 so it is its own section in
  the heading outline.
- Test that "Not updated only" survives a year switch that keeps the open
  call in view, and that the table leaves a controlled true alone there.
- Drop issue numbers from two test comments.

commits.message:
feat(misc#392): undo an answer and read its history in the questionnaire (#740)

* feat(misc#392): undo an answer and read its history in the questionnaire

Adds the UI for the revisions API (CMS-Enterprise/ztmf#596): an Undo button in
the strip that already holds the carry-forward chip and Confirm, and a View
history drawer off the "Last edited by ..." caption showing revisions
newest-first with who, when, kind, and a before -> after comparison.

The drawer is the app's first Drawer; the theme's MuiDrawer override had never
been exercised. It is not an extension of ScoreDiffModal - that modal is
cross-data-call, per-system and all-questions, and its scrim would hide the
answer being compared against. What they share is the before/after cell, which
is extracted verbatim from its renderSide; ScoreDiffModal.test.tsx passes
unmodified, which is the proof the extraction preserved behaviour.

Undo eligibility is never re-derived here. The server marks each revision
undoable or not and supplies the reason string; the client renders it verbatim,
so the rules have one home.

canUndoAnswer requires state === 'updated', and that clause is load bearing:
undoing the first edit of a carried-forward answer returns status to
not_started, which re-arms Confirm, so without it both buttons would render at
once. undoState.test.ts proves the two are never simultaneously true across the
whole state x flag matrix.

scores.status joins priorReviewContextId, because the prior-response review
gate reads that column. Without it an undo could not re-arm the review, and a
CMS system's blank-box + "Insert into response" presentation would only
reappear after navigating away and back - the same answer looking different
depending on how you reached it.

useAnswerHistory reads history per answered question rather than on drawer
open: the Undo button renders off the head revision's undoable flag, so gating
the read on the drawer would mean the button could never appear. It also
refreshes on the row's edit stamp, so Undo shows the instant a save lands
rather than on the next navigation, which keeps saveResponse and
confirmScoreById byte-identical as the issue requires.

The four QuestionnairePage suites gain a QueryClientProvider rather than moving
to renderWithProviders: that helper hardcodes MemoryRouter, which the deeplink
suite explicitly rejects in favour of a data router.

yarn test 1245 passing, tsc and eslint clean, make frostfall-local clean with
the baseline untouched.

* fix(misc#392): give the history drawer dialog semantics

aria-labelledby sat on the Drawer root, which MUI renders with
role="presentation" - that strips semantics, so the label was discarded and the
panel announced as nothing, with no role and no aria-modal anywhere. Dialog
applies both to its own Paper automatically; Drawer does not.

axe does not flag a missing dialog role on a custom panel, so the green
frostfall scan was never evidence this was right. Pinned by a test asserting
the dialog role, aria-modal, and the accessible name.

Also: notes render with whiteSpace pre-wrap, so a multi-paragraph justification
no longer collapses into one run-on block. Pre-existing in the diff modal but
newly load-bearing, since with redo gone the drawer is the only way to read a
prior note back after an undo. And undoState's doc no longer claims redo stays
reachable from the drawer - ztmf#596 marks undo heads not-undoable outright.

* feat(misc#392): describe what the Undo button restores

The label is three words, so a screen-reader user was told an action exists
and nothing about the value it lands on. The button now carries an
aria-describedby preview - "Restores the answer "Traditional" and its
justification, saved 3 March 2026." - following the CARRY_FORWARD_HELPER_ID
pattern already in this page.

Hidden rather than visible: the restored value is already on screen in the
drawer row, so repeating it beside the button would be noise for sighted
users. The three-word label is only a problem for someone who cannot see the
row it acts on.

Built entirely from data already on the client. The head projection carries no
sides, but head.prev is by definition the `new` side of the revision below it,
and that row's createdat is when the value being restored was saved - so no API
change. undoPreview returns undefined when the option cannot be named, and the
button then emits no describedby at all rather than pointing at empty text.

The drawer's head row now renders the shared UndoAnswerButton rather than its
own copy, so the two cannot drift on label or description.

* fix(misc#392): drop the now-dead onViewHistory prop from LastEditedFooter

The trigger moved out of LastEditedFooter during the rebase - the redesign
demoted that component to a Tooltip title, where a link is hover-only. With
the link living beside SaveIndicator instead, nothing passes onViewHistory,
so the prop and its Box/Link branch were dead. Reverted to main's version;
its nine tests pass unchanged.

* test(misc#392): pin the HHS presentation after undoing a carried-forward answer

The CMS variant had a page-level undo test; the non-insights variant did
not. Undo must land on carried text in the box with the helper copy and
Confirm, not on the CMS blank-box review.

* fix(misc#392): address review on undo and answer history

- Refetch history when an undo 403 is auth-handled, so a past-deadline
  Undo button doesn't linger
- Let admins undo from the drawer on a closed call, matching the
  server's deadline bypass
- Move focus to View history after a successful undo from the strip
- Make the drawer's scrolling body a focusable, labelled region
- Re-arm the prior-response review when an undo restores only the notes

commits.message:
feat(opdivs): per-OpDiv and all-OpDiv maturity dashboard under /opdivs (#748)

* feat(opdivs): per-OpDiv and all-OpDiv maturity dashboard under /opdivs

Adds a dashboard at /opdivs/:opdivId and an aggregate at /opdivs/all, and
promotes OpDivs to a nav tab for every admin read tier. The management grid
moves to /opdivs/manage; /admin/opdivs becomes a legacy redirect.

The OpDiv is a client-side filter rather than a request parameter, so
switching OpDivs costs no network traffic and the blocking score/progress
queries share cache keys with the main dashboard.

Also lands the shared FE infrastructure the page needs: src/api/scores.ts and
src/api/users.ts query hooks, a single param shape behind
apiPaths/queryKeys.scores.aggregate, the generic presentational components
promoted to components/ui/, a daysUntil helper, and a ?opdiv= deep link into
the Users table.

Refs #745

* refactor(opdivs): drop the unused FismaTable OpDiv-lock props

lockedOpDivId and hideDecommissionedToggle were added for an earlier design
that embedded a systems table on the OpDiv dashboard. That page deliberately
carries no table - the main dashboard already holds the full enumeration - so
nothing consumes either prop.

Refs #745

* feat(opdivs): one score-range tile, a confirm backlog tile, and visible jumps

Highest and Lowest were two tiles spending one fact. On a small scope they
name the same system twice, and with nothing scored they are two em-dashes
side by side. They are one Score range tile now, sitting immediately beside
the hero because it finishes the sentence the hero starts: an average says
nothing about whether the systems behind it cluster or straddle three tiers.

Each end of the range carries its own tier color. Painting the pair uniformly
throws away the thing a range exists to show, and the tile this replaced was
worse - it gave every lowest score the fixed "down" color, so an estate
sitting entirely at Optimal rendered its floor as an alert. The tier is named
in the hint too, so the reading never depends on telling two fills apart.

The freed slot becomes Answers to confirm: systems carrying last cycle's
answers that nobody has confirmed. They read as answered everywhere else and
still register no progress (ztmf#659), so they are the cheapest work on the
page - confirming is not re-answering. It is a subset of Not started rather
than a sibling, and its explanation says so.

Jumping from a tile to its panel now rings the target for two seconds and
hands it focus. Scrolling alone left the keyboard caret back on the tile, so
the next Tab continued through the summary rather than into the panel just
opened, and a screen reader was told nothing had happened.

Refs #745

* feat(opdivs): let capped panel lists open in place

Every worklist caps how many systems it names, which kept the cards a
readable height but ended them on a dead sentence: "and 14 more not started."
is precisely the point at which someone wants the other fourteen, and the
panel's whole purpose is to hand off into the work.

Not started, Risk, Score by system and both coverage lists now carry a Show
all control that reveals the remainder in place. Expanding rather than linking
elsewhere, because the rows are already on the client and each one already
links to its system - sending the reader to a filtered table would cost a page
load to reach links they were one click from.

The hidden count rides in the control's accessible name, so a screen reader
hears what opening it will reveal rather than a bare "show all".

Refs #745

* fix(opdivs): cap how far a panel list expands

Expanding revealed the whole list, which is fine for the risk and coverage
lists but wrong for Not started: at the start of a data call every enrolled
system is on it, and at CMS scale that is over a thousand rows. A thousand
nodes inside a summary card is neither readable nor worth the DOM.

Expanding now stops at fifty and says what it left out, pointing at the
systems table for the rest. The four panels share one useExpandableRows hook
rather than each keeping its own collapsed/expanded arithmetic, so the panels
carry less code than before this change.

Refs #745

* fix(opdivs): paint the score range from the accessible tier palette

The Score range tile took its color from tierDot, which is documented as
accent dots that sit BESIDE a value rather than as text - and several of its
shades fail WCAG AA as a foreground. Advanced (#C19A00) is 2.66:1 on white,
missing even the 3:1 large-text bar, and Not Assessed (#9AA3B2) is 2.54:1.

Frostfall caught it on #749, not here, because the scan covers the dashboard
and these tiles only reached it once the summary band landed there. The
violation it captured is a gold "4.00" - an Advanced range.

TIER_CHIP_STYLES is the accessible source of truth the token file points at,
and clears 4.5:1 on every tier, so the value is painted from that instead. The
em-dash and the zero-count neutrals move off neutral400 (2.54:1) to
neutral500 (5.97:1) for the same reason.

scoreRange.test.ts computes the ratios rather than restating hexes, so a later
shade change fails there instead of in a 508 scan.

Refs #745

* fix(opdivs): address review findings on the OpDiv dashboard

Follow main's #741: order pillars as the API serves them (pillarOrder)
instead of reviving the deleted client-side rank.

- Prior call follows the scope's cadence, so a delta is never computed
  against a call the OpDiv did not run.
- daysUntil counts to the deadline instant the backend enforces.
- Risk counts a system unknown when either impact flag is unrecorded.
- Questionnaire saves and confirms invalidate cached scores.
- Not-started links use questionnairePath, not the acronym route.
- Users ?opdiv= filter is always visible and clearable, and resets.
- Deactivating an OpDiv no longer redirects back to it.
- Load failures render an error state instead of zeros or false empties.
- No all-zero flash when arriving with decommissioned on.
- Switcher moves out of the h1 and shows an inactive OpDiv.
- Export omits fsids for a whole-scope export; disables when the URL
  would exceed CloudFront's limit.
- Settings saves identity before the delegate toggle and no longer
  reseeds mid-save; Add system hidden on inactive OpDivs.
- A11y: tooltips describe their buttons, visible focus, h2 regions,
  trend table and live readout, contrast.
- Reuse ui/Eyebrow, Stat, TrendLine; mono hero; hooks move to src/utils;
  drop dead exports, unused barrel entries and the duplicate Card.

* test(opdivs): condense the dashboard tests into the page and one derivations file

Panel-level tests are folded into OpDivDashboard.test.tsx where the
behaviour matters, and the eight logic suites merge into
opdivDerivations.test.ts.

* fix(opdivs): address review feedback on the OpDiv dashboard

Review items:
- Trend chart clicks select the point again: recharts 3 passes the
  index as a string, and counts it from the brush window
- Stage donut drops the recharts keyboard layer inside its role="img"
- User, grant and delegate writes invalidate the cached user list
- Cache-sharing comments describe Home's current state accurately
- Zero data calls renders an empty state instead of a spinner
- summarizeTargetGap is covered by tests
- Aggregate subtitle counts OpDivs from the returned systems
- Export tooltip no longer promises an exact count when unfiltered
- ChartCard describeChild comment gives the right reason

Found in follow-up review:
